RUNTIME-ONLY fields (underscore-prefixed, CLAUDE.md §1's "a live reference never survives save/reload" rule): `binds[i]._live` (the resolved live Paper Path) is SET at two places in this scope — rigBindStroke's own bind literal (2118, `_live:path`) and relinkRigBinds' filter (1951, `b._live=item`) — and never persisted: exportJSON's own ld.rig.binds map (timeline.js:2163) and cloneRigForSymbol's identical map (app.js:3245) both list only `{strokeId,meshId,rest,restHandles,weights,rotate}`, omitting `_live`/`_liveRaster` entirely by construction (a hand-written field whitelist, not a delete-before-stringify step) — timeline.js's own comment (2145-2153) states this was previously copied wholesale into JSON.stringify (a 2026-07-30 fix, corrected here), which risked throwing mid-save on Paper's own circular internal references. `binds[i]._liveRaster` (the resolved live Raster) is SET at rigBindMesh's own bind literal (2186, `_liveRaster:raster`) and relinkRigBinds' filter (1946, `b._liveRaster=ras`) — same never-persisted disposition, same two whitelists confirmed to omit it. packets.responsibility: Step 2 of the Rig tool's own 3-step flow (draw bones, auto-assign, pose), per Cyril's spec cited directly (2026-07-29, "un bouton d'assignation qui assigne automatiquement les éléments du layer sélectionné aux bones"). Binds EVERY selectable shape AND every meshed image on the layer against EVERY bone in one pass, relying on rigBindStroke's/rigBindMesh's own per-bone-radius weighting to produce a sensible "nearest bone wins, blended near a boundary" result without per-shape bone selection — and REPLACES whatever binds already existed (via rigBindStroke's/rigBindMesh's own replace-not-stack rule), so re-running this after adjusting an influence circle is the expected "try again" gesture, not something that piles up stale binds (2145-2154). `boneIds=Object.keys(rig.bones)`; a bare `return 0` (NOT the normal `{n,skippedUnsupported}` shape) if there are no bones at all — a return-shape inconsistency, see `boundaries`. AUTO-SIZING the fallback radius (2026-07-29 fix, "l'autoassign marche pas alors que j'ai mis les bones sur la shape") is the largest single block: since the per-vertex weight is a LINEAR falloff hard-clamped to 0 past the radius, and the fixed 200px default is narrower than half the width of any shape over ~400px (the common case for a torso/limb on a 1920x1080 canvas), auto-assign used to create a bind that visibly did nothing when posed — indistinguishable from "doesn't work" to the artist (2192-2205). The fix scans every selectable PATH's own vertices once (nested `layer.children.forEach` × `c.segments.forEach` × `boneIds.forEach`, each iteration allocating and immediately removing a throwaway `_boneSegsToPath`, packet 2) and grows `neededRadius` to the farthest one actually needs — but ONLY for a bone that doesn't already have its own manually-set `bone.radius` (`if(!bone||bone.radius)return;`), so a bone the artist already resized via its own influence circle keeps that manual radius untouched. Mesh vertices count toward the SAME measurement (2026-08-30 addition, 2222-2226): a second, structurally identical triple-nested scan over every meshed Raster's own world-mapped vertices, guarded by `typeof Raster!=='undefined'&&window.SMImageMesh&&window.SMEngineBridge&&SMEngineBridge.rasterImageRect` — skipping it would reproduce, for images, the exact 0-weight-edge bug the path scan exists to fix. A small margin (`Math.ceil(neededRadius*1.05)`) ensures the single farthest vertex gets a sliver of pull instead of landing exactly on the falloff's own zero boundary. `skippedUnsupported` counts every `CompoundPath` child encountered in the paths loop — rigBindStroke's own guard already rejects a CompoundPath (no single `.segments` to bind), counted HERE so the caller can surface an honest toast instead of a silent "0 forme(s) assignée(s)" (2251-2256). `wantPaths`/`wantMeshes` (2026-08-30, "oui mais faut avoir le choix") are independent opt-outs, both defaulting to on via `!opts||opts.X!==false`, so a layer with both a drawing and a meshed image can be rigged to drive either, both, or neither kind of content. The MESH loop runs BEFORE the PATHS loop (both gated by their own `want*` flag inside their own forEach, not hoisted above it). The paths loop's own trailing comment (2275-2286) states explicitly why a vector-brush ribbon's linked-fill companion is NOT independently bound here: its own sparse 2-point centerline geometry can't represent an arbitrarily bent multi-joint curve the way the ribbon's many finely-sampled boundary points can (QA-confirmed live: a visible mismatched red sliver cutting across the bend) — applyRigDeform (C21i, cited by name only) instead copies the ribbon's OWN already-correctly-deformed boundary onto the companion after every deform, guaranteeing an exact match by construction rather than a second, independently-approximated deformation that can diverge. Returns `{n,skippedUnsupported}` from its normal exit.
